chain: (1) DATO: Rin 102.88 / 143.26 / 143.03 Mohm, tau 18.55 / 18.79 / 21.25 ms, rest -79.25 / -75.51 / -73.62 mV (34634460 Table 1; O01-O03). -> (2) INFERENZA: tau flat while Rin rises 39 percent argues against a PURE leak loss at constant capacitance (predicted tau about 25.8 ms against 18.8 and 21.3, about 3.9 and 2.9 SE below); this holds under the single-compartment assumption and a hyperpolarisation-activated conductance in the 50-60 ms fit window could also shorten the apparent tau, so it supports "something besides a pure leak loss", not specifically "smaller cells". -> (3) INFERENZA: implied capacitance tau/Rin about 180 / 131 / 149 pF reproduces but carries about 14 percent propagated uncertainty (WT versus HT z about 1.6, WT versus KO about 1.1) and does not follow the dose order: a lower capacitance in mutants is a direction of means, not an established difference. A smaller cell with unchanged specific resistance gives Rin up and tau flat; it does not by itself depolarise rest, but smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak (A10) would give Rin up, rest depolarised and tau flat, so the depolarised rest needs a second cause (fewer open K+ channels, seal or recording factors, or network state, MH3). -> (4) INFERENZA: with a fixed -200 pA step the larger Rin drives HT and KO cells about 8 mV further (about 20.6 versus 28.7 mV), to peaks of about -101, -106, -105 mV on the recorded scale, so absolute sag and rebound in mV can rise with no change in HCN. -> (5) INFERENZA: E_K is about -97 to -98 mV and needs no junction correction; the recorded potentials do (about -13 mV, borrowed): on the corrected scale the peaks are about -114 / -119 / -118 mV, 16-21 mV BELOW E_K, so K+ current at the sag peak is inward and not small; the prediction that a K-leak difference current reverses near E_K belongs to the voltage-clamp experiment E3 (zero crossing at the corrected E_K), not to the sag peak. -> (6) benefit: none claimed; a measurement hypothesis that decides whether any pharmacological arm is needed for the sag at all.
pharmacological_action: None proposed. A leak or Kv7 opener would hyperpolarise and lower Rin in wild-type and mutant cells alike, so a response would not show a leak deficit (a drug response is not proof of a defect in its target).
compound_or_probe: None nominated. Kv7 openers (retigabine: abstract states KCNQ2, KCNQ3, KCNQ2/3 and KCNQ4, not KCNQ5, and native M channels in rat sympathetic neurons; SCR2682: abstract names rat hippocampal or cortical neurons) were read at abstract level only; XE991 was not read; K2P and Kir tool papers exist (reported by the verifier: ML133 for Kir2 and ML335/ML402 for TREK-1/TREK-2 in heterologous systems, not read by me) but none is shown to work in layer II/III pyramidal neurons. No compound is justified on this basis.
context: Mouse neuron-specific Synapsin-Cre Wwox deletion, layer II/III pyramidal neurons, P13-P17 acute slices at 35 C, littermate Cre+ controls; endpoint: sag, rebound and Rin at matched potential and matched deflection, capacitance, tau, Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive current; no exposure (ex vivo).
competing_explanation: MH2 (an HCN contribution that remains after matching); A05 recording factors (access resistance, selection by Rin and tau); A10 smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak; A04 maturation delay; A06 network state.
counter_evidence: F-I slope unchanged (O09) is a constraint not explained; sag fraction still rises in crude group means (5.4 to 8.2 percent) but with about 1.6 propagated SE between WT and KO, so it is not established; the HT-versus-KO difference in sag (t about 0.9) and rest (t about 0.8) is NOT used against MH1 (not distinguishable); flat tau may be a protocol artefact (tau and Rin from different protocols).
weakening_result: Matched potential and matched deflection (or a Rin-normalised sag ratio) removes the genotype difference in sag and rebound AND voltage-clamp capacitance is lower in mutants AND Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive current per pF is unchanged -> passive size explains most of Rin and sag; the reading fails if sag remains at matched conditions (MH2), if capacitance is unchanged while Rin is higher, or if the Ba2+-sensitive difference current does not reverse near the corrected E_K in the E3 voltage-clamp experiment. Smaller-cell versus seal-leak versus leak loss is separated by E1 plus E3 only if seal and access resistance are reported.
discriminating_experiment: E1 (matched-potential, matched-deflection, Rin-normalised sag, with Ra and capacitance reported) plus E3 (K-leak reversal near E_K, junction potential corrected).
status: survives as an exploratory, qualitative hypothesis (flat tau against pure leak loss is supported; implied capacitance, step 5 as first written and the HT-KO gradient were weaker than written and are corrected here); no Wwox conductance datum exists; decisive probes are abstract level or unread
what_would_change_the_decision: A measured capacitance and tau in the same cells; a Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive current in Wwox neurons; or evidence that access resistance differs by genotype (which would move weight to A05).

chain: (1) DATO: sag 1.18 / 2.04 / 2.57 mV and rebound 0.96 / 1.24 / 1.86 mV at a fixed -200 pA (O04, O10); the authors infer an elevated Ih from the larger deflection (O11); no voltage-clamp Ih exists. -> (2) INFERENZA, premise NOT established: a residual sag excess after matching would indicate a larger HCN contribution or shifted gating; the crude sag fraction 5.4 / 6.6 / 8.2 percent carries about 1.2-1.6 points of propagated uncertainty (WT versus KO z about 1.6, WT versus HT about 0.7), Ih activation is steeply voltage dependent so a fraction can rise with unchanged HCN density when the step reaches 4-5 mV deeper, and the HT-versus-KO difference at equal estimated deflection is not distinguishable (t about 0.9); the premise is UNVERIFIABLE without per-cell sag, Rin and deflection. -> (3) DATO (transfer): an HCN blocker REDUCES sag in normal cortical layer 5/6 neurons (ivabradine, 34018186, rat 25-35 d, Fig 5 viewed: about 2.65 to about 1.4 mV at -200 pA, n=6) and in thalamic neurons (ZD7288 20 umol/L, 24953239: residual 0.4-2.1 mV from 4-6 mV, with a 15-18 mV hyperpolarisation), so HCN contributes to sag in those cells; DATO at abstract level: ZD7288 also blocks T-type current (extracellular application, CA1) and sodium current (DRG, Nav1.4). -> (4) INFERENZA: a second chemotype plus a voltage-clamp subtraction can assign an excess sag to Ih; without both it cannot (the thalamic authors themselves note possible T-type window-current contamination of the ZD7288-subtracted current). -> (5) benefit: unknown in direction; an increased Ih is not assumed harmful. The GAERS authors expect Ih-driven burst suppression to be seizure-reducing, discuss a compensatory origin and then say any compensation is unlikely to be directly related to SWD development; they do not call the Ih rise harmful; in GAERS more Ih came with lower peak-based Rin, unchanged rest and unchanged sag (A09), not the Wwox pattern.
pharmacological_action: HCN blockade as a TOOL arm in slices (two chemotypes, engagement first), reading sag, rebound, Rin, rest and burst incidence in the same slices; no candidate drug and no in-vivo claim.
compound_or_probe: Tool classes only: ZD7288 (sag reduction and hyperpolarisation read in 24953239 full text, Fig 6 viewed) and ivabradine (sag reduction and hyperpolarisation read in 34018186 full text, Fig 5 viewed; described by the authors as a nonselective inhibitor of HCN isoforms). Not nominated as treatments; ivabradine in vivo needed an efflux inhibitor to reach about 184 nmol/L free brain level (n=4), and the slice concentrations were micromolar.
context: Mouse neuron-specific Wwox deletion, layer II/III pyramidal neurons, P13-P17, acute slices 35 C, bath exposure of the tool at a concentration verified for engagement; endpoints: ZD7288- and ivabradine-sensitive sag at matched conditions, Ih density per pF and V1/2 in voltage clamp, then burst incidence.
competing_explanation: MH1 (passive and leak reading); T-type contribution to rebound (Z944 arm, hcn_20261107 X4); sodium-current off-target of ZD7288; a different HCN isoform or compartment.
counter_evidence: GAERS (24953239): more Ih with lower peak-based Rin, unchanged rest and sag; ZD7288 lowered Rin (authors: unexpected) at a 15-18 mV more negative potential. Neocortical ZD7288 study cited by 34634460 reported Rin up (secondhand; its abstract, 27464853, gives no such numbers). Review (37982354) says open HCN lowers Rin; Wwox Rin is up. A blocker-mediated sag reduction does not show an HCN defect.
weakening_result: At matched potential and deflection the sag and rebound excess disappear, or ZD7288- and ivabradine-sensitive current per pF and V1/2 are the same in KO and WT -> no HCN difference; MH2 retained only as a statement that HCN contributes to sag as it does in normal cortex. Sag reduced by a blocker with burst incidence unchanged supports HCN in sag, not benefit; burst incidence rising is not by itself compensation either.
discriminating_experiment: E1 then E2 (voltage-clamp Ih isolation with ZD7288 and a second chemotype), then E4 (blocker arms with bursts), as in hcn_20261107 X1, X2, X4, X5.
status: survives only as a conditional, exploratory hypothesis: its premise (a residual excess sag at matched conditions) is not established and is testable only with matched data (E1); rests on abstract-level or untested items for the decisive datum (no Ih in Wwox cells; ZD7288 off-target numbers abstract level; Kv7 and T-type probes abstract level); the Fig 5 reading confirms a partial sag reduction, not abolition
what_would_change_the_decision: A matched-condition excess sag in KO that is blocked by both chemotypes, together with a larger voltage-clamp Ih density, would move HCN from "contributes" to "differs"; absent that, no HCN-directed compound is ranked.

chain: (1) DATO: neocortical slices burst spontaneously in 36 of 42 KO, 4 of 23 HT and 0 of 11 WT slices (O08); intrinsic properties were recorded in cells that were not spiking spontaneously (O07). -> (2) INFERENZA: the Methods "Pharmacology" paragraph lists only TTX, d-APV, carbenoxolone and brilliant blue FCF and no AMPA or GABA-A antagonist, so the intrinsic recordings were most probably unblocked (not an explicit statement). Synaptic shunting would LOWER Rin (INFERENZA); an effect of raised [K+]o on Rin is IPOTESI (Kir and rectification can act in either direction), so the higher Rin argues against a pure activity-driven state but does not exclude one. -> (3) INFERENZA: HT shows the Rin and rest changes with bursting in a small fraction of slices (the cells are not linked to slices in the paper), but HT slices also differ from WT in mEPSC statistics (pooled-event KS tests, Fig 4 legend), so a synaptic state without bursts is not excluded. -> (4) DATO: pyramidal identity was confirmed using Rin and tau, the outcomes themselves; access resistance up to 40 Mohm was accepted against a Rin of 100-143 Mohm. -> (5) INFERENZA: a selection-independent, maturation-matched comparison under synaptic blockade is the precondition for reading MH1 and MH2; persistence under blockade would show that the difference is intrinsic to the recorded neuron membrane, not that Wwox acts cell-autonomously (the Cre is pan-neuronal; that needs sparse or mosaic deletion). The cell-context axis (layer, maturation stage) remains open. -> (6) benefit: none; it protects the interpretation of pharmacological arms.
pharmacological_action: None. It is a design-control hypothesis: repeat the intrinsic-property measurements under synaptic blockade, with identity by morphology or marker, Ra and bridge balance reported by genotype, and an age series (for example P10 to P17) plus layer V.
context: Same mouse model and slices; additional contexts: layer V pyramidal neurons, an age series around P13-P17, and recordings in WT versus KO slices under synaptic blockade and with unblocked synaptic transmission.
competing_explanation: MH1 or MH2 as genuine cell-autonomous differences; A04 maturation delay (predicts smaller sag); A07 cell-type mix.
counter_evidence: HT changes with little bursting; F-I slope unchanged; but no datum on blockade (beyond the probable absence of blockers), identity by morphology or access resistance by genotype exists in the paper.
weakening_result: Under synaptic blockade, with identity by morphology or marker and matched access resistance, the genotype contrast in Rin, rest and sag is unchanged -> the difference is intrinsic to the recorded membrane and independent of selection; if it shrinks or vanishes, the original contrast was partly synaptic state or selection. Wwox cell-autonomy is not tested by this experiment.
discriminating_experiment: E1 variants (blockade on and off; Ra, capacitance and bridge reported; biocytin identity) and E5 (age and layer series).
status: survives as a design control, strengthened: the probable absence of synaptic blockers in the intrinsic recordings is an inference from the Methods drug list, not a stated fact; exploratory
what_would_change_the_decision: An explicit statement from the authors that intrinsic properties were recorded with or without synaptic blockers (the Methods list is only indirect evidence); recordings under blockade with matched access resistance; sparse or mosaic deletion for cell-autonomy.
